items.title: Live: Reserve Bank hikes cash rate to 4.1 per cent; Treasurer says it will bring extra 'pressure' for Australians
items.description: The Reserve Bank has raised the cash rate to 4.1 per cent, its second hike in as many months as inflationary pressures continue. Follow the latest updates in our live blog.

items.title: 'We haven't seen anything yet': China's plan to kick foreign oil habit
items.description: China is adopting green energy at a scale hard to imagine for many other countries, with the country's latest five-year plan further signalling its intention to reduce its dependency on foreign oil.

items.title: Farmers urged to increase security amid spike in fuel thefts
items.description: The NSW Police Rural Crime Team is reporting a spike in diesel being stolen from landholders amid soaring prices.

items.title: Fuel crisis forces gold miner to send two-thirds of workers home
items.description: Fuel shortages linked to the Middle East war are forcing a WA gold miner to halt operations and stand down workers, exposing how smaller operators are being squeezed while major miners maintain supply.

items.title: Live: Trump scolds allies for failing to help secure Strait of Hormuz, says 'level of enthusiasm' matters
items.description: The US president hits out at European allies, who he says "weren't that enthusiastic" about helping, as Iranian drones and missiles closed the shipping channel. Follow live.

items.title: An 'incredible unease' now hangs over the UAE as war creates new normal
items.description: Amid Iran's missile and drone attacks, a weird sense of normality in Dubai and Abu Dhabi sits awkwardly with the news coverage of burning buildings and reports of strikes on airports.

items.title: What to know about travel insurance cover amid Middle East war
items.description: War-linked travel disruptions remain largely excluded under standard travel insurance policies, experts say.

items.title: Even America's critics often speak its language
items.description: For much of the past century, the world has learned to interpret war through categories shaped by American power.

items.title: After one chat with a stranger, 30 years of two families' histories came crashing down
items.description: When Sasha Szafranski matched with a stranger on a genealogy website, she uncovered an IVF mix-up that had been hidden for 30 years.

items.title: Bondi gunman's family living in fear, court told
items.description: A lawyer has revealed Naveed Akram's mother and siblings have been targeted with abusive messages, death threats, stalking and pork chops being thrown into their driveway.

items.title: 'We have exciting days ahead': Danish royals arrive in Melbourne
items.description: The king and queen of Denmark will arrive in Melbourne for the first of two days of royal engagements as part of their Australian state visit.

items.title: From fire to flood, how climate change contributed to summer of whiplash weather
items.description: Scientists warn sharp swings from extreme heat to flooding rain experienced over summer are a sign climate change is overtaking other weather drivers.

items.title: Petrol price rise amid war in the Middle East adds to cost-of-living focus in SA state election
items.description: Increased costs for petrol, food and housing are front and centre when it comes to how families are choosing to vote in the upcoming South Australian state election.

items.title: Afghanistan accuses Pakistan of deadly airstrike on drug rehab centre
items.description: There are fears of heavy casualties as Afghanistan accuses Pakistan of hitting a treatment centre for drug addicts in the capital, Kabul, and killing civilians.

items.title: Why — and how — I'm taking a break from my husband
items.description: After almost five decades of marriage, I needed a break. And since enjoying my new-found freedom, I'm not sure I'll ever go back.

items.title: Timothée Chalamet's Oscars campaign was DOA before he dissed ballet
items.description: At the beginning of 2025, Timothée Chalamet was the hot pick for the Best Actor Oscar for his turn in Marty Supreme. But a lot can change in a few months.

items.title: ABC Places quiz: Where in the world are we?
items.description: Today's ABC Places quiz features photos from 10 locations around the world. Your challenge is to guess where you are.

items.title: It's sitting on 303 billion barrels of oil but no one wants to extract it
items.description: Foreign Correspondent goes inside Venezuela's oil regions, where boom towns have gone bust, leaving behind a shattered industry that needs billions to reboot.

items.title: New lines of enquiry into mysterious Albany death in 1991
items.description: WA detectives have travelled to the Great Southern city of Albany to re-investigate the hit-and-run death of Mark Edward Gregory in 1991.

items.title: Bluesfest collapse 'gut-wrenching' for supplier left $65k out of pocket
items.description: The merchandise suppliers were due to deliver more than 6,000 T-shirts and other branded items this week to be sold at the famous Byron Bay festival over Easter.

items.title: Tasmanian government responds to scathing transparency review
items.description: Tasmanian cabinet documents would be proactively released after 20 years under reforms proposed by the state government in response to a scathing review of the state's Right to Information system.

items.title: Towns pick up pieces after loss of Commonwealth Games that should have started today
items.description: The 2026 Victorian Commonwealth Games would have started today, but attention now turns to the unbuilt housing and unfinished regional projects that were promised.

items.title: Islamic school could be deregistered if principal is not sacked
items.description: An education standards investigation finds social media commentary by the principal of an independent Islamic school in southern NSW was of a "concerning and hateful tone".

items.title: Adrift Russian tanker poses serious risk of 'major ecological disaster'
items.description: Italy, France and seven other nations say a Russian liquefied natural gas tanker adrift in the Mediterranean represents an ecological threat, urging swift action.

items.title: Beachgoers warned to keep their distance after cliff collapse
items.description: A South Australian mayor says no-one was hurt when boulders fell from a cliff face at a popular beach in Adelaide's south.
